newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico PRI wants to ensure post-poll budget - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico PRI wants to ensure post-poll budget - report.

text.p: Mexico's ruling party congressmen, likely to take a beating in elections next week, are manoeuvering to pass 1998's budget early, Reforma newspaper said on Friday.

The paper cited Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) members of Mexico's lower house of Congress as saying they were planning to convene a number of special sessions that would allow them to pass next year's budget before the new chamber met in September.
The budget would normally be presented to Congress between September and November 15, the constitutional deadline.
The idea would be to guarantee President Ernesto Zedillo the same budget in 1998 as in 1997, plus a rise to compensate for inflation, Reforma said.
"They said they were already working on the terms of the reform so as to be prepared in the 'remote event' that the PRI loses its majority in the elections on July 6," it said.
Mexicans are electing a full lower house of Congress in next week's vote. Several polls have showed the long-ruling PRI, for the first time in its history, is unlikely to retain its majority.
Such a reform would not entail any constitutional change and therefore would not require opposition approval. The PRI has a large majority in the outgoing congress.
The paper also quoted Chamber of Deputies sources as saying that since last week members had been forbidden to travel abroad.
"That is way of guaranteeing their presence in the country should a period of extraordinary sessions be called," one source said.
